questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.

  • In the first blank the most appropriate conjunction is 'when'.
  • We use when as a conjunction meaning ‘at the time that’.
  • The clause with when is a subordinate clause (sc) and needs a main clause (mc) to complete its meaning.
  • If the when-clause comes before the main clause, we use a comma.
    • Example: (SC)When I was young, (MC)there were no houses here.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.​

So the complete passage is:- I have always enjoyed flying. I wasn't afraid (1) when my mother and I boarded LANSA Airlines flight 508. Some people had (2) given up flying LANSA because of a recent crash. But (3) mother and I had a good reason for flying: I had just (4) finished secondary school in Lima, and we wanted to (5) spend Christmas with my father in our jungle hut. 

Additional Information

  • What is a Conjunction? 
    • A conjunction is a word that connects or joins clauses, words, phrases together in a sentence.
    • Conjunctions are used to coordinate words in a sentence.
    • Three types of conjunctions are Coordinating Conjunctions, Subordinating Conjunctions, Correlative Conjunctions.

Key Points

  • "Rare" (दुर्लभ) means something that is not common or frequent.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: Sudden changes in the gilts market are rare, but when they do happen it can cause (2) _________ problems for certain types of pension scheme, as UK pension savers (3) ________ recently. In addition to raising borrowing costs for the government, the market mayhem following September's mini-budget (4) _________ many pension providers to quickly cash in some of their holdings to try to weather the (5) _________ .

Additional Information

    • "Easy" (आसान) usually means something that can be achieved with no difficulty. 
    • "Severe" (कठोर) refers to something very great; intense. It usually describes the intensity or degree of something, not its frequency.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Key Points

  • The correct answer is "have seen".
  • The context of the sentence is in the present perfect tense, which is used to express an action that happened at an unspecified time before now.
  • The present perfect tense is formed with "have/has" + past participle.
  • Here, the past participle of the verb "see" is "seen".

Therefore, the correct sentence is: Sudden changes in the gilts market are rare, but when they do happen it can cause major problems for certain types of pension scheme, as UK pension savers have seen recently. In addition to raising borrowing costs for the government, the market mayhem following September's mini-budget (4) _________ many pension providers to quickly cash in some of their holdings to try to weather the (5) _________ .

Additional Information

  • Let's now look at the other options:
    • "Seen" - This is the past participle of "see", but without "have" or "has" before it, it doesn't fit the sentence grammatically.
    • "Has seen" - "Has" is used for third person singular subjects. However, "UK pension savers" is plural, so "have" should be used instead of "has".
    • "Did saw" - This is incorrect because "did" is the past of "do", and it should be followed by the base form of the verb, which would be "see", not "saw".

    • "Slated" generally means scheduled or planned for a certain time. This does not fit in the context because the act of cashing in their holdings was a reaction to market conditions, not something that was scheduled or planned.
